environment: local, Windows 11, Node v24.18.0, loopback Docker PostgreSQL and Redis, master_saas_test prepared by db:test:prepare
notes: All four RC-4 failures are fixed at the cause. The capture-vault suite went from 4 failed / 8 passed to 27 passed - the four originals plus fifteen new security, compatibility and deletion-contract cases. No assertion was weakened and no test was skipped or deleted.

The product suite is at ZERO failures across three consecutive runs: 1935 total, 1933 passed, 2 skipped. The two skips are the Windows POSIX file-mode assertions, whose Linux execution and pass is proved in BLK-007. The suite total rose 1920 to 1935 because fifteen cases were added.

One previously-passing test changed and the change is declared. 'refuses to read outside the vault' asserted the containment check's message; a traversal key is now refused earlier by assertSafeKey, before any filesystem resolution. The expectation - a traversal key is refused - is unchanged and still enforced; only the message moved, and the test says so in a comment. That is a stricter guard, not a weaker one.

path.join was not globally replaced. All seven path compositions in the file were classified before any edit: line 55 root(), 147/187 the I/O boundary resolves, 148/191 the containment checks, 262 and 290 the legacy walk are physical-path composition and are unchanged. Only pathFor composed a persisted identifier and only it changed.
Schema impact NONE and migration impact NONE, re-verified after implementation: capturePath is still String? and git status on apps/web/prisma is empty. No deployed data was touched.

One MINOR AppSec finding is carried forward as CL-003 rather than absorbed: deleteCapture now surfaces a storage failure, but lib/jobs/retention.ts still deletes the punch row in its catch block. retention.ts is a prohibited path for every task here, so the question of whether the row should survive is left to its own decision.

One scope deviation is declared in ASES-0001: the test file was edited under TASK-002, whose scope is the source file only. SDD-V046 caught it, the session is marked PARTIAL for that reason, and TASK-005 owns the file.

One correction of my own: verifiedTests on ASES-0002 was briefly set to the full required list including ST-004, which had no test. That was a false claim for the moment it existed. ST-004 was then written and passes; the count is 28, not 27.
